They also include the unknown/malformed id test, the refusal while a writer holds the case, the retries after an interrupted purge and after a failed ledger write, and the 8-thread ledger race.

findings.claim: Another writer that is waiting for the case while a purge holds it recreates the case folder after the purge. The hardener fixed this for a second purge by passing create=False (store.py:741), but store._recorded (store.py:303), used by update_profile and import_file, still calls log.writer() with create=True. Each retry of _enter runs self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) and opens the .gate and .lock with O_CREAT. So once the purge has renamed the folder and released the lock, the waiting writer makes a new cases/<id>/ holding the two lock files. mkdir uses its default mode, so the folder is not forced to 0700. The writer then fails (no case.yaml, or no inputs/ or statements/ folder), so no statement or profile data comes back. But a folder named by the case id is left behind after the ledger says the case was purged, and purge_target (store.py:681-684) no longer finds it, because it has no case.yaml and no .purging- prefix, so purging again cannot clean it up.
findings.repro: Hold case.for_case(folder).writer() in thread P and call store.update_profile(folder, f) in thread B, so B retries inside writer(). In P, os.replace(folder, folder.parent / ('.purging-' + id)), delete its contents and release. B's next _enter calls mkdir at case.py:842 and creates cases/<id>/log.jsonl.gate and log.jsonl.lock. B then raises on load_profile. Afterwards os.path.isdir(cases/<id>) is True, and store.purge_case(id) answers 'no case'.

findings.claim: A ledger append that is cut off part-way, by a crash or a short write on a full disk, leaves a line with no newline. The next purge's O_APPEND write then joins its own record onto that fragment. _ledger_records (store.py:765-776) skips the joined line as invalid JSON (suppress(ValueError)), so the later case's record is unreadable and its dedupe check misses it. A retry then appends a duplicate. os.write's return value is also not checked for a short write.
findings.repro: Write '{"case":"aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa","pur' (no newline) to purge_ledger.jsonl, then purge case B. The ledger's last line is the fragment followed by B's JSON, and json.loads fails on it. Purge B again from an unfinished .purging- mark and a second line for B is appended.

findings.claim: Claim note (1) says two fully concurrent purges can still both append, and that a lock on the ledger would be needed. The final commit 0044b3f already adds that flock (store.py:657-669), and test_purges_finishing_together_record_the_case_once covers it, so the note is stale and misdescribes the shipped code. Claim 1 also cites '12 passed', but the file now has 13 tests. The runner's logs show all 13 ran and passed.
